headline: Exploited flaws in Apache, NGINX and Synology need patching as CISA sets a November 21 deadline
plain_summary: Several widely used server products have flaws that attackers are already using or that have public attack code, including Apache HTTP Server, Apache Roller and NGINX. CISA gave US agencies until November 21 to fix four exploited flaws. Microsoft's Agent Framework package on PyPI carried a credential stealer for a short time. Equinor's cyberattack is still being handled; production is unaffected and no attacker is named. Teams running these products should check and patch.

items.title: CISA adds four exploited flaws to KEV; three due November 21
items.why: Synology DSM, LiteLLM, Apache Axis and REDCap flaws are confirmed as exploited, with US federal deadlines starting November 21.
items.action: Check for Synology DSM, LiteLLM, Apache Axis and REDCap in your environment, apply vendor fixes, and keep LiteLLM and REDCap off the open internet until patched.

items.title: Exploitation reported for Apache HTTP Server mod_http2 flaw
items.why: Singapore's CSA says exploitation is reportedly under way and proof-of-concept code is public.
items.action: Find Apache HTTP Server 2.4.55 to 2.4.70 with mod_http2 enabled and update to the latest release at once, internet-facing servers first. Check the Apache advisory for the full list of affected versions.

items.title: Apache says Roller remote code execution flaw is exploited
items.why: An unauthenticated flaw in the XML-RPC interface is being used in attacks against versions 4.0.0 to 6.1.4.
items.action: Upgrade Apache Roller to 6.1.6 or later. If you cannot, set enabledForExtensions to false in WEB-INF/web.xml, remove the /roller-services/xmlrpc mapping and restart; switching off XML-RPC in the admin UI is not enough.

items.title: NGINX HTTP/2 flaws allow remote code execution; public PoC
items.why: CERT-FR knows of a public proof of concept for one of two unauthenticated remote code execution flaws.
items.action: Check every NGINX Open Source and NGINX Plus server that serves HTTP/2. Apply the fixed versions from F5 bulletins K000163926 and K000163928, or disable HTTP/2 until patched (remove http2 from the listen line, or set http2 off on 1.25.0 and earlier). Review exposed servers for signs of compromise.

items.title: CISA urges immediate patching of Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938)
items.why: A critical Java flaw could allow unauthenticated remote code execution, and Oracle's November update fixes it.
items.action: Find every Java runtime, including ones bundled in third-party apps, containers and appliances. Apply Oracle and vendor patches, internet-facing systems first. Until patched, validate and size-limit Base64 input and restrict unauthenticated access.

items.title: Microsoft Agent Framework PyPI package carried a credential stealer
items.why: Versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2 ran a stealer at Python start-up and targeted cloud, GitHub and AI credentials.
items.action: Check for Agent Framework 1.26.1 or 1.26.2 in environments and CI builds, pin to 1.26.0, and rotate Azure, AWS, GitHub, Docker, Hugging Face and OpenAI credentials and OIDC tokens on any host that installed them.

items.title: Around 40 Irish credit unions affected by supplier breach
items.why: Saved payee records were exposed at supplier Wellington IT; passwords, PINs and card details were not.
items.action: Credit union members should watch for payment fraud and phishing that uses saved payee details. Credit unions should confirm what Wellington IT holds for them and ask it for access logs.

items.title: NSA Net outage: agency cites maintenance, no cyberattack indicated
items.why: The NSA attributes the classified network outage to routine maintenance, and the Director of National Intelligence said there is no sign of a coordinated cyberattack.
